subject: Future Tech
title: Lunar Water Ice
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Lunar Water Ice.

hook.text: In 2009, NASA crashed a rocket into a lunar crater and confirmed water ice hiding in the permanent shadows.

buildup.text: The Moon's poles have craters so deep that sunlight never reaches the bottom.

discovery.text: That ice can be melted for drinking, split into oxygen for breathing, and hydrogen for rocket fuel. Triple value.

twist.text: Extracting ice in permanent shadow means working in extreme cold and total darkness with robotic miners.

climax.text: NASA's VIPER rover, planned to explore these craters, will map ice deposits and test extraction methods on-site.

punchline.text: Lunar ice is water, air, and fuel all in one.

quiz.question: Where on the Moon is water ice found?
options: In permanently shadowed craters at the poles
